Feature: Is there an overt marker for the absolutive?
curated_comment: Absolutive (S and P) has zero marking; only the ergative agent is overtly marked with -te. No overt absolutive marker. Value 0 confirmed (Campos 2009:§8.1.3, examples 50-65).

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging on first person pronouns?
curated_comment: 1st person agent takes ergative marker -te in transitive clauses: ex. (85) 'Ã -te mã ax' (1sg.AG ERG eat FUT) = 'Eu comerei'. Corrected from 0 to 1 (Campos 2009:146, ex.85).

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging on second person pronouns?
curated_comment: By paradigmatic analogy with 1st and 3rd person: if -te marks transitive agents for all person categories, 2nd person should also take -te. No direct 2nd person example found in PDF pages 137-146; requires additional verification of other sections of Campos 2009.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging on third person pronouns?
curated_comment: 3rd person NPs and pronominal A arguments take ergative marker -te throughout: ex. (50) 'Ũn -te kakxop xi-nãhã' (woman ERG boy eat-CAUS), (53) 'Tik -te xapup...' (man ERG pig...). Corrected from 0 to 1 (Campos 2009:§8.1.3, examples 50-65).

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging on full NPs?
curated_comment: Full NPs in A (transitive agent) position consistently take the ergative marker -te throughout the grammar: ex. (50-65). S (intransitive subjects) lack -te. Classic ergative flagging on full NPs. Corrected from 0 to 1 (Campos 2009:§8.1.3).

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in the imperfective aspect?
curated_comment: The -te ergative marker appears to apply regardless of aspect; no imperfective/perfective split is documented in the available pages. Corrected from 0 to 1 pending further verification of aspect-specific data in Campos 2009.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in the perfective aspect?
curated_comment: Perfective transitive clauses (past/completed events) consistently show -te on A: examples (50-65) describe completed events. Corrected from 0 to 1 (Campos 2009:§8.1.3).

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in the past tense?
curated_comment: Past/completed transitive clauses show -te on A throughout examples (50-65). No tense-conditioned split documented. Corrected from 0 to 1 (Campos 2009:§8.1.3).

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in non-past tenses?
curated_comment: Future (non-past) transitive clauses also show -te: ex. (85) 'Ã -te mã ax' (1sg.AG ERG eat FUT) = 'Eu comerei'. No tense split. Corrected from 0 to 1 (Campos 2009:146, ex.85).

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in the indicative mood?
curated_comment: Indicative mood transitive clauses consistently show -te on A across many examples. Corrected from 0 to 1 (Campos 2009:§8.1.3, examples 50-65).

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in non-indicative moods?
curated_comment: Non-indicative (future/irrealis) transitive clauses also show -te: ex. (85) 'Ã -te mã ax' (1sg.AG ERG eat FUT). No mood-based split. Corrected from 0 to 1 (Campos 2009:146, ex.85).

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in the realis status?
curated_comment: Realis transitive clauses show -te on A throughout examples (50-65). Corrected from 0 to 1 (Campos 2009:§8.1.3).

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in the irrealis status?
curated_comment: Future marker -ax may correspond to irrealis status; transitive future clause (85) shows -te on A. Corrected from 0 to 1, requires further verification of full irrealis paradigm (Campos 2009:146, ex.85).

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in the context of an agentive A?
curated_comment: Agentive A arguments (canonical volitional agents) take -te throughout: ex. (50) woman feeds boy, (53) man fattens pig, (63) grandmother makes food. Corrected from 0 to 1 (Campos 2009:§8.1.3).

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in the context of a non-agentive A?
curated_comment: Insufficient data in available pages to confirm whether non-agentive A (e.g., experiencer, stimulus) also takes -te. Value remains 0 pending further verification of Campos 2009 chapters on semantic role conditioning.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in the context of a topical A?
curated_comment: Insufficient data to determine topicality conditioning. Requires discourse-pragmatic analysis sections of Campos 2009. Value remains 0 pending verification.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in the context of a non-topical A?
curated_comment: Insufficient data to determine non-topical A marking. Requires discourse-pragmatic analysis sections of Campos 2009. Value remains 0 pending verification.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in the context of an animate A?
curated_comment: Animate A arguments (human agents: woman, man, boy, grandmother, etc.) consistently take -te. Corrected from 0 to 1 (Campos 2009:§8.1.3, examples 50-65).

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in the context of an inanimate A?
curated_comment: Inanimate A argument attested with -te: ex. (57) 'Yip -te kuxa-nõ-a kãmãnok' (jipe/car ERG heart-end-CAUS horse) = 'o carro assustou o cavalo'. Corrected from 0 to 1 (Campos 2009:140, ex.57).

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in main clauses?
curated_comment: Main clauses consistently show -te on transitive agents throughout §8.1.3 examples. Corrected from 0 to 1 (Campos 2009:§8.1.3).

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in non-main clauses?
curated_comment: Insufficient data in available pages to confirm ergative alignment in subordinate/non-main clauses. Value remains 0 pending verification of relative clause and complement clause sections in Campos 2009.

Feature: Is ergative alignment of flagging conditioned by any other factor?
curated_comment: No evidence of additional conditioning factor beyond transitivity. The -te marker appears to apply consistently to all transitive agents. Value 0 may be correct but requires full cross-chapter verification of Campos 2009.

Feature: Are the ergative and the genitive expressed by the same marker?
curated_comment: No evidence in available pages that -te also marks genitive. Maxakalí uses relational nouns (inalienable possession with person prefixes) for possessive marking, not the -te suffix. Value 0 likely correct (Campos 2009).

Feature: Are the ergative and the instrumental/comitative expressed by the same marker?
curated_comment: No evidence in available pages that -te marks instrumental or comitative. Value 0 likely correct pending full verification (Campos 2009).
